title: tryLDG OOB operand read / crash on invariant atomic load (AtomicSDNode misclassified as MLoad)
trigger: A global-space atomic load that is invariant. Realistic compiler-generated path: a CUDA kernel reading a 'const __restrict__' (readonly noalias) pointer with an atomic load -> NVPTXTagInvariantLoads adds !invariant.load -> tryLoad -> canLowerToLDG true -> tryLDG OOB. Also reproducible directly by attaching !invariant.load to a load-atomic. Confirmed at -O0, default, and -mcpu=sm_70.

title: printHexu32imm misprints prmt selectors with bit 31 set as malformed negative hex (e.g. -0x1U instead of 0xffffffffU)
trigger: @llvm.nvvm.prmt with an immediate selector that has bit 31 set (selector >= 0x80000000), e.g. -1 / 0xFFFFFFFF / 0x80000000 / 0xFFFF0000. Lowers to prmt.b32 ... , <printed-as-negative>U.

title: tryBFE GoodBits uses i32 shift-amount width instead of i64 value width (missed-opt only, NOT a miscompile)
mechanism: In the first AND path of tryBFE, after Start = LHS->getOperand(1) (the shift-amount operand), the code computes `GoodBits = Start.getValueSizeInBits() - StartVal`. NVPTX::getScalarShiftAmountTy returns MVT::i32 unconditionally (NVPTXISelLowering.h:104), so Start.getValueSizeInBits() is always 32, even when the value being extracted (Val = LHS->getOperand(0)) is i64. It should use Val.getValueSizeInBits() (64). Because the only use of GoodBits is the guard `if (NumBits > GoodBits) return false;`, underestimating GoodBits (32 vs 64) makes the guard TOO STRICT: it rejects valid i64 bitfield extracts whose start bit is >= ~16 (e.g. (and (lshr v,40),0xFFFF)). This is a MISSED OPTIMIZATION, not a miscompile -- when the transform does fire the bound is always within the correct 64-bit range, so the emitted bfe is always correct. I include it only for completeness; it does not meet the correctness-bug bar.
trigger: i64 value of the form (and (lshr/ashr v, K), mask) where K + popcount(low-mask) <= 64 but > 32 - it falls back to shr+and instead of bfe.u64/bfe.s64. Result is correct, just unoptimized.

title: replaceImageHandle: image/texture/surface handle reaching the access via an unhandled def (e.g. select -> SELP) hits default llvm_unreachable
mechanism: replaceImageHandle() finds the def of the handle vreg via `MachineInstr &TexHandleDef = *MRI.getVRegDef(Op.getReg());` and switches only on four opcodes: LD_i64, texsurf_handles, nvvm_move_i64, and TargetOpcode::COPY. Everything else falls into `default: llvm_unreachable("Unknown instruction operating on handle");` (line 1834-1835). The texture/surface handle is a plain i64 SSA value, and the intrinsics (e.g. llvm.nvvm.tex.unified.1d.v4f32.s32, llvm.nvvm.suld.1d.i32.trap) accept any i64. If the i64 handle is produced by a select (selecting between two texsurf.handle.internal results, or any other i64), the reaching def after ISel is a SELP_b64 (not LD_i64/texsurf_handles/move/COPY), so the switch reaches the unreachable. This is valid, non-UB IR: `%h = select i1 %c, i64 %h0, i64 %h1` then used as the texture/surface handle. The same firing path also leaks via the recursive COPY/move case which forwards getOperand(1) to a SELP def. Because this is llvm_unreachable (not report_fatal_error), in a release/NDEBUG build it lowers to __builtin_unreachable() (UB / corrupt codegen), not a graceful diagnostic; in an assertions build it is a hard abort. Either way it is a backend crash reachable from well-defined input rather than a 'cannot select'/unsupported-op diagnostic.
trigger: A CUDA-target NVPTX kernel that forms a texture or surface handle (i64) with a `select` and passes it to a tex.unified / suld / sust intrinsic. The select lowers to SELP_b64, whose opcode is not in replaceImageHandle's switch.
ir:
target triple = "nvptx64-unknown-cuda"

declare { float, float, float, float } @llvm.nvvm.tex.unified.1d.v4f32.s32(i64, i32)
declare i64 @llvm.nvvm.texsurf.handle.internal.p1(ptr addrspace(1))

@tex0 = internal addrspace(1) global i64 0, align 8
@tex1 = internal addrspace(1) global i64 0, align 8

define ptx_kernel void @sel(ptr %red, i32 %idx, i1 %c) {
entry:
  %h0 = tail call i64 @llvm.nvvm.texsurf.handle.internal.p1(ptr addrspace(1) @tex0)
  %h1 = tail call i64 @llvm.nvvm.texsurf.handle.internal.p1(ptr addrspace(1) @tex1)
  %h = select i1 %c, i64 %h0, i64 %h1
  %val = tail call { float, float, float, float } @llvm.nvvm.tex.unified.1d.v4f32.s32(i64 %h, i32 %idx)
  %ret = extractvalue { float, float, float, float } %val, 0
  store float %ret, ptr %red
  ret void
}

title: Internal (local-linkage) ptx_kernel with a byval parameter: assert(!isKernelFunction) fires; in release the kernel's byval param is silently over-aligned to >= 16
file: llvm/lib/Target/NVPTX/NVPTXUtilities.cpp (assert line 51, returned value line 52); reached from NVPTXSetByValParamAlign.cpp:67 and NVPTXAsmPrinter.cpp:1414/1430
trigger: An `internal` (or `private`) function with `ptx_kernel` calling convention (or kernel metadata) that has a `byval` parameter. Valid IR: the verifier accepts it.

title: PerformSELECTShiftCombine drops overflow guard on non-i64 shift when the guard compare is on a wider amount (miscompile)
mechanism: PerformSELECTShiftCombine recognizes a guarded shift `(select (ugt amt, BW-1) 0, (shift x, amt))` (and the ULT/SHL forms) and rewrites it to NVPTXISD::SRL_CLAMP/SHL_CLAMP, relying on PTX shr/shl clamping shift amounts >= BitWidth to 0. The shift amount used in the rewrite is `ShiftOp.getOperand(1)` (line 6768-6769), and the matchers permit a width mismatch between the guard's compared value and the shift's amount: (a) the shift amount is matched with `m_TruncOrSelf(m_Deferred(ShiftAmt))` (lines 6745-6746), so the actual shift amount may be a *truncation* of the (wider) ShiftAmt that the icmp tested; (b) the guard constant is matched with `m_SpecificInt(APInt(BitWidth, BitWidth-1))`, and m_SpecificInt uses APInt::isSameValue which compares values irrespective of bit width (SDPatternMatch.h:1335), so `icmp ugt i64 %s, 31` matches even though BitWidth (the SELECT/shift type) is 32. Result: for an i32 shift guarded by a 64-bit comparison, the combine deletes the guard entirely and emits a bare `shr.u32`/`shl.b32` that consumes only the low 32 bits of the 64-bit amount (the param is loaded with `ld.param.b32`). When the high 32 bits of the amount are nonzero but the low 32 bits are < the shift width, the guard would have produced 0 but the emitted code shifts by the (small) low bits instead. The fix should require the icmp's compared value and the shift's amount to be the same SDValue (no trunc), and the guard constant width to match the shift width. Distinct from the listed i64 bug #3 (which is about an i64 *destination* shift's 32-bit amount register); here the destination shift is i32/non-i64 and the defect is the cross-width matching that fires the combine at all, matching the assignment's hint about '32-bit-amount truncation for non-i64 wide types'.
trigger: i32 (or other non-i64) logical shift whose overflow guard compares a wider (i64) amount, e.g. C like `unsigned long n; uint32_t r = (n > 31) ? 0 : (x >> (uint32_t)n);`. Concretely with x = 0xFFFFFFFF and s = 0x100000000 (= 2^32): correct result is 0 (since 2^32 > 31), but emitted PTX computes `x >> low32(s) = x >> 0 = 0xFFFFFFFF`. Verified against x86_64 llc which keeps the full-width guard (`cmpq $32,%rsi; cmovbl`). Fires at all SM versions and at default -O2 (no OptLevel guard in the combine).
ir:
define i32 @guarded_shift_wide(i32 %x, i64 %s) {
  %st = trunc i64 %s to i32
  %c = icmp ugt i64 %s, 31
  %sh = lshr i32 %x, %st
  %r = select i1 %c, i32 0, i32 %sh
  ret i32 %r
}

define i32 @guarded_shl_wide_ult(i32 %x, i64 %s) {
  %st = trunc i64 %s to i32
  %c = icmp ult i64 %s, 32
  %sh = shl i32 %x, %st
  %r = select i1 %c, i32 %sh, i32 0
  ret i32 %r
}

title: Inline-asm register-class selection ignores value type: a value wider than the constraint's register class is silently truncated (i64/f64/ptr with 'r' loses the high 32 bits)
trigger: Use a 32-bit constraint ('r' or 'f') on a 64-bit operand (i64, double, or pointer), or more generally any constraint whose register class is narrower than the operand. Reachable from C/CUDA via clang too: clang's validateAsmConstraint (clang/lib/Basic/Targets/NVPTX.h ~125) accepts r/l/etc but performs NO width checking, so asm("...":"=r"(x)) with a 64-bit x compiles silently.

title: llvm.minimumnum/maximumnum lowered to bare PTX min/max — wrong signed-zero result (minimumnum(-0.0,+0.0) returns +0.0 instead of -0.0)
lines: 1092-1100 (PatFrags fminnum_or_fminimumnum / fmaxnum_or_fmaximumnum and defm MIN/MAX); enabled by NVPTXISelLowering.cpp:1044-1055 setting FMINIMUMNUM/FMAXIMUMNUM Legal
trigger: Any llvm.minimumnum.* or llvm.maximumnum.* where one operand is -0.0 and the other is +0.0 (or any equal-magnitude opposite-signed-zero pair). E.g. minimumnum(-0.0f, +0.0f): defined result -0.0, NVPTX yields +0.0.

title: Inline-asm 'r'/'f' (B32) constraint on f64: only the low 32 bits of the double reach the asm; e.g. 2.0 becomes 0.0
mechanism: Same root cause as the i64 case but with a floating-point operand, and notable because the data loss is in the *most significant* half. For double the constraint 'r'/'f' selects B32 (RegVT=i32). The generic FP-into-int branch (SelectionDAGBuilder ~10100) only triggers when RegVT.isInteger() && ConstraintVT.isFloatingPoint() AND it then uses MVT::getIntegerVT(ConstraintVT.getSizeInBits()) = i64, but that path is gated by the earlier 'equal size' check having already failed; for f64 (64 bits) into i32 (32 bits) the sizes differ, so ConstraintVT becomes i64 and RegVT stays i32, again giving RegsForValue(i32-reg, i64-value): the f64 is bitcast to i64 then truncated to its low 32 bits. llc emits 'ld.param.b32 %r2, [f_param_0]' loading only the low word of the 8-byte double, then 'cvt.u64.u32' zero-extends. For a double whose low 32 bits are zero (e.g. 2.0 = 0x4000000000000000, 1.0 = 0x3FF0000000000000), the value seen by the asm and returned is 0.0.

title: Sub-byte vector params (<N x i1>) emit out-of-bounds param stores/loads, corrupting values and adjacent params
mechanism: For a parameter of type <N x i1>, the PTX .param storage is declared with size DL.getTypeAllocSize(<N x i1>) = ceil(N/8) bytes (e.g. 1 byte for <2..8 x i1>). But ComputePTXValueVTs (lines 308-331) flattens the vector via ComputeValueVTs into N separate scalar i1 entries, then in the i8-handling block forces RegisterVT=i8 and assigns Offsets[I] = Off + I*RegisterVT.getStoreSize() = 0,1,2,...,N-1. The comment at lines 324-327 explicitly flags this: "This is horribly incorrect for cases where the vector elements are not a multiple of bytes (ex i1) ... no one has complained." LowerFormalArguments (line 4155-4159) then loads each element with VecAddr = ArgSymbol + Offsets[I] (i.e. param+1, param+2, ...), and LowerCall (line 1609-1623) stores at the same offsets. Both the caller's store loop and the callee's load loop access bytes 0..N-1 of a param declared with only ceil(N/8) bytes, i.e. up to N - ceil(N/8) bytes past the end of the .param slot. In the PTX param state space each .param declaration is independent fixed-size storage, so these accesses are out-of-bounds; ptxas behavior is undefined and may silently corrupt the adjacent parameter slot or read garbage, producing a result different from the well-defined IR semantics.
trigger: Any function with a <N x i1> argument where N >= 2 (so N > ceil(N/8)), as caller and/or callee. Confirmed: <2 x i1>, <4 x i1>, <8 x i1>. Valid, non-UB IR.

title: Scoped atomic min/max intrinsics (int_nvvm_atomic_{max,min}_gen_i_{cta,sys}) always lower to signed PTX (.s32/.s64); unsigned CUDA atomicMax_block/Min on unsigned values is miscompiled
mechanism: ATOM2_minmax_impl<OpStr> emits TWO instruction patterns for the SAME intrinsic family: `defm _s32 : ATOM2S_impl<OpStr,"i","s32",...>` (-> atom.max.s32) and `defm _u32 : ATOM2S_impl<OpStr,"i","u32",...>` (-> atom.max.u32). Both pass IntTypeStr="i", so ATOM2N_impl builds op = int_nvvm_atomic_max_gen_i_{scope} for BOTH. There is only ONE such intrinsic (IntrinsicsNVVM.td:1918 `defm int_nvvm_atomic_max_gen_i : PTXAtomicWithScope2<llvm_anyint_ty>` — overloaded on int type, carrying NO signedness). ISel therefore always picks the first/signed pattern. Verified: the intrinsic always emits `atom.cta.max.s32`/`.s64` and the .u32/.u64 instructions are dead. This is an end-to-end miscompile, not just an ambiguous-IR nitpick: clang routes BOTH signed and unsigned builtins to the same intrinsic — clang/lib/CodeGen/TargetBuiltins/NVPTX.cpp:618-622 lists __nvvm_atom_cta_max_gen_i (signed) AND __nvvm_atom_cta_max_gen_ui (unsigned) both -> Intrinsic::nvvm_atomic_max_gen_i_cta; clang/test/CodeGen/builtins-nvptx.c:463 (signed) and :466 (unsigned) both CHECK `call i32 @llvm.nvvm.atomic.max.gen.i.cta.i32.p0`. So CUDA `atomicMax_block`/`atomicMin_block`/`atomicMax_system`/`atomicMin_system` on `unsigned`/`unsigned long`/`unsigned long long` compile to a SIGNED max/min. (By contrast the non-scoped atomicrmw path correctly uses distinct atomic_load_max vs atomic_load_umax SDNodes.) Concrete: *p=0x80000000, v=1: unsigned max must yield 0x80000000 (2147483648 > 1) but atom.max.s32 yields 1 (1 > -2147483648). Affects min and max, 32- and 64-bit, both cta and sys scopes.
trigger: Call llvm.nvvm.atomic.max.gen.i.cta.i32 (or .min / .sys / .i64) — i.e. CUDA __nvvm_atom_cta_max_gen_ui / atomicMax_block(unsigned*) — on a value whose unsigned and signed orderings differ (high bit set), e.g. existing 0x80000000 vs argument 1.

title: Inline-asm 'b' (predicate/B1) constraint on a wide integer truncates the value to its least-significant bit
mechanism: case 'b' returns B1RegClass (RegVT=i1) regardless of operand type. An i32 operand under 'b' is forced into a 1-bit predicate: the generic code's only same-size/FP repairs do not apply (i32 vs i1, both int, sizes differ), so the i32 is truncated to i1. llc emits 'and.b32 %r3, %r2, 1; setp.ne.b32 %p1, %r3, 0' before the asm, i.e. the asm sees only bit 0 of the input. Any i32 value v becomes v&1. Note 'b' (and 'N','0') are NOT among clang's accepted NVPTX constraints (NVPTX.h validateAsmConstraint), so this is reachable via handwritten LLVM IR / non-clang frontends rather than C, but is still a silent backend miscompile of valid IR.
trigger: Constraint 'b' applied to any integer wider than i1.

title: Inline-asm constraint whose register class is WIDER than the operand emits width-mismatched PTX (ld.param.b32 into a .b64 register; st.param.b32 from a .b64 register)
mechanism: For an i32 operand under the 'l' (B64) constraint, getRegForInlineAsmConstraint returns B64 (RegVT=i64). The generic code places the i32 in RegsForValue(i64-reg, i32-value). Because the value is *narrower* than the reg, no truncation occurs, but the emitted PTX declares the register as .b64 (%rd) while the load/store of the 32-bit param uses .b32 width: llc produces 'ld.param.b32 %rd2, [f_param_0]' and 'st.param.b32 [func_retval0], %rd1' where %rd1/%rd2 are .b64 registers. PTX requires the data-type suffix to match the register width, so ptxas rejects this; the backend has emitted malformed output for valid IR. (The same VT-ignoring root cause as the truncation findings, but here the symptom is invalid PTX rather than a wrong value.)
trigger: A constraint whose register class is wider than the operand, e.g. 'l'/'d'/'N' on an i32, or 'q' on anything smaller than i128.

title: FTZ applied to fpext f16/bf16 -> f32 flushes the (sub)normal narrow input, miscompiling exact widening conversions to 0.0
trigger: Compile `fpext half to float` (or `fpext bfloat to float` on sm_90+) with FTZ enabled, i.e. the f32 denormal mode = preserve-sign (clang passes -denormal-fp-math-f32=preserve-sign for -fcuda-flush-denormals-to-zero / fast-math). Input = any f16 subnormal, e.g. half 0xH03FF = 6.097555e-05. Correct result: 6.097555e-05 (a normal f32). Emitted code computes cvt.ftz.f32.f16 -> +0.0.

title: FTZ applied to llvm.ceil/llvm.floor/froundeven f32 flushes subnormal input, changing the rounded result (e.g. ceil(subnormal) yields 0.0 instead of 1.0)
mechanism:
multiclass CVT_ROUND maps fceil/ffloor/froundeven/ftrunc to integer-rounding cvts, and under doF32FTZ uses the *_FTZ mode:
  def : Pat<(OpNode f32:$a), (CVT_f32_f32 $a, ModeFTZ)>, Requires<[doF32FTZ]>;
defm : CVT_ROUND<fceil, CvtRPI, CvtRPI_FTZ>;  // -> cvt.rpi.ftz.f32.f32
The `.ftz` flushes the subnormal f32 input to sign-preserving zero BEFORE the round-to-integer. For llvm.ceil.f32 of a tiny positive subnormal (0 < x < smallest normal), the correct result is +1.0, but FTZ flushes x to +0.0 and ceil(+0.0)=+0.0. Similarly floor of a tiny negative subnormal: correct -1.0 vs FTZ-flushed -0.0 -> 0.0. This is a value change for a well-defined input. Weaker than finding #1 because the input genuinely is f32, so flushing it is arguably the intended (if surprising) consequence of the user-selected f32 FTZ mode; reported for completeness.
trigger: Compile `call float @llvm.ceil.f32(float %a)` with FTZ enabled (-denormal-fp-math-f32=preserve-sign). Input = a positive f32 subnormal, e.g. 0x00000001 (~1.4e-45). Correct ceil = 1.0; emitted cvt.rpi.ftz.f32.f32 yields 0.0.
